summary:
plan.md is written: 8 modules, each kept inside its 12x14 plot. Each plot has the pad's spruce fence and gate, a slab-then-2-long-landing way in, and a chimney set into the wall with its stack behind the house, clear of the back fence.
Each building has one feature that names it from the lane: the gin's yellow board front gable with a wagon door, hoist beam and an empty machine bay with a marked shaft; the white school with its bell cupola; the farmhouse with a deep porch; the open-fronted forge; the church steeple (to about y 26, the one the village sees); the tall vented tobacco barn; the slatted corn crib; and the brick owner's house (copper roof, wraparound porch, bay, back balcony facing downhill).
Block ids passed mcd blocks --check; no roof dry-run, fit, approach or render has been run yet. Eight-module Polarton row on a 12x14 plot grid: gin, school, farmhouse, smithy, church, tobacco barn, crib/granary and owner's house. All use the architect's coordinates, slab-ramp ways in, and exterior chimneys with hearths at the bottom.
elements.md and the plan.md sections (PALETTE, VOCABULARY, ROOMS, PARTS, NOTES) are written. Six parts: two shells, roofs, fittings, hearths and stairs, grounds.

shells plots 0-3: Shells for gin, schoolhouse, farmhouse and smithy: plinths, walls, posts, beams, floors, gin shaft frame and port, all openings and reserved cells left unwritten. make.sh clean with no refused or off-palette blocks.

Farmhouse back wall cells x33..34 z14 are open until the chimney is built
Did not run mcd fit or render the tiles

summary:

Left the vent open; the stairs/fittings trade must pick one. The ladder helper also needs (63,3..9,14) solid if the ladder stays.

Church lancet stair-heads: the stairs at z14 and z16 for the lancet at z15 would sit at y7; I kept (56,7,16) solid so the tower ladder's wall (x56, z16) holds. Lancet at z15 therefore gets only one head stair on the east wall; the lancet helper will refuse the z16 stair there.
Tower decks at y8 and y15 (x52..53 z10..11 hole area) are left air for the stairs/tower part; the nave floor at y8 under the tower shaft is not built.

Not built (other parts): church cornice ring y18 and spire (roofs), altar round window and gable walls above y7 (roofs), lancet sills/heads and tower round window (fittings), belfry louvres come from belfry() but are unverified in render, graveyard picket and headstones (grounds), granary double door and loft door, crib front hatch (fittings), owner lintels/sills/porch/balcony (porch and fittings), owner back-wall chimney mouth (chimney part).

waste.cost: about 3 minutes of reasoning, plus one rebuild
waste.tool: A plan check that lists each helper's cells against the shell's leave boxes and reports conflicts (a lancet stair cell vs a ladder wall, a vent vs a ladder back) before anything is written.

waste.what: Checking the render: zooms of three areas, read by eye, to confirm walls and openings read as the plan describes.
waste.cost: 3 zoom renders
waste.tool: A `$MCD fit`-style report that flags an opening that is shut or a required wall that is missing, so the check does not need a render.

Set the lancets (sills, glass, stair heads) and the bay glazing, using the openings I left as air, with the stair-head cells at z14/z16 settled first.

summary:
roofs: parts/roofs.mjs lays the main roofs of all eight plots (roof() per building, keep boxes for stacks and the cupola), plus the farm porch shed, forge and barn lean-tos, the schoolhouse cupola cap and the church spire (spireCap). make.sh writes a whole build.nbt.
The roofs are not trussed, and the gin's monitor, owner porch roof and cupola bell/louvres are not built. 48 roof cells on the gin's side eave are refused by the shell, and many roof stairs are off-palette.
Chose per-building roof() calls over roof.json, since runParts takes one spec for all eight styles; no roof.json is written.
polish: Gin eave: 48 roof writes refused at x=1 (and x=10), y=9, z 9..16: the shell leaves the wall-top course there as air, so the gin's side eave has a hole; fix in shell-a (close the y9 head plate at x1/x10) or accept the gap.

Off-palette stairs/slabs from the roof tool's default trim and mix edges: stripped_spruce_log_stairs x59, dark_oak_stairs x53, oak_stairs x65, oak_slab x45, deepslate_brick_stairs x19, polished_andesite_stairs x10 and similar. Needs explicit eave/trim/hips keys in every material mix, or a palette-only roof vocabulary.
Trusses not built: no trusses key or truss simulation run, so no tie beams, purlins or king posts under any roof.
Gin ridge monitor with louvres (plan ROOFS row 0) not built; gable louvre is P4's.

Schoolhouse cupola: only a stepped cap ring and the lightning rod at (17,18,14) are built; the cone is not the spec's lantern-cap form, and the bell (17,15,14) and louvres are not placed (P2/P5). The rod may sit one course off the apex; check in the render.
Owner's house porch roof (low copper hip wrapping the corner, plan ROOFS 7 porch) not built; porchWrap and porchDeep in P4 write their own roofs, which will collide with P3 cells if they overlap.
Farm porch shed is a rough row of stairs and slabs (z7..9, y6); the stair/slab pattern is not verified against the loft window or the body wall.
Cart lean-to (forge) and stripping-shed lean-to are single stair rows: no posts, no ridge and no verge; the lean-to posts belong to P1/P6.
Rendered once (front, street, iso): roofs read as roofs, but nothing was looked at close up and the wall-top course was not checked with mcd fit or mcd check beyond the orphan list (none from roofs).

waste.what: Worked out each building's footprint, ridge line and keep-box coordinates by hand from the ROOFS table, then re-checked them against the render.
waste.cost: about 8 roof calls and 3 lean-to loops written by hand; 4 rebuilds to see refusals
waste.tool: A roof table reader: mcd roof --spec per building in plan.md ROOFS, or a roof-spec JSON emitter that takes the table row and writes the call.

waste.what: Chose a material mix per roof by hand to keep it in the palette, then found the tool's default trim/eave/hips still pulled in off-palette stairs and slabs.
waste.cost: 4 full make.sh runs to read the OFF-PALETTE line; several guesses at mix keys
waste.tool: roof() option that takes palette role names (slate, spruce-shingle, copper) and derives eave, trim, hips and verge from the palette.json roles, with no free-form ids.

waste.what: Used a stepped cap ring written cell by cell for the cupola instead of a helper.
waste.cost: about 40 set() calls in a nested loop
waste.tool: lantern-cap or bellCupola cap call with a rod option, as in vocab h1, instead of hand stepping.

waste.what: Searched the roof tool's source for rectangle conventions and option keys (rectsOf, roof(), presets).
waste.cost: about 6 greps and reads across roofs.mjs and the roofs reference
waste.tool: A one-page roof-spec reference in the crew folder: the keys, the rect convention (inclusive x0,z0,x1,z1), and the preset defaults.

companions.task: Design the king-post and queen-post trusses and purlins for the cottage, church nave, barn and gin roofs, then hand the timber list to the roofer to lay.
Hand-build the porch shed, the cart and stripping-shed lean-tos and the cupola stepped cap so each stair faces the right way and the lean-tos meet the walls.
Place the cupola bell, its louvres and its lightning rod against the spec, and check the spire's rod and cross sit on the apex.
Close the gin's side head plate at y9 on x1 and x10 so the roof's eave course can land without refusals.

summary:
openings and ways in: parts/fittings.mjs writes every plot's glass, doors, shutters, vents and louvres, the wagon and hay doors, hoist beam, lancets, porches (porchDeep, porchWrap), owner balcony, and the slab ramps with landings (school, farmhouse, church, granary, owner).
make.sh runs clean and writes build.nbt. The openings part places 536 cells and refuses 26 writes into shell cells (the gin wagon lintel and folded leaves, and others not listed), and reports calcite_stairs as off-palette (now stone_brick_stairs).
Checked: `mcd fit` shows no bottom-slab floats after the lancet sill became a top slab. Its 51 "floating shutter" flags are the intentional in-wall vent slots and louvres, not errors. I looked at the farmhouse and owner zooms; the porch and ramps read as intended.
polish: Gin wagon bay: the lintel at y5 x3..8 and the folded leaves at x2..3 and x8..9 (y1..4, z9) are refused because the shell owns those wall cells. The shell should leave them open or write the stripped_spruce_log lintel itself.

26 writes refused in total; the report lists only 8 of them. Likely the rest are lancet stair heads at y7 in the nave wall and the belfry louvres at the tower, which may duplicate P2's belfry. Not individually confirmed.

Church door lintel uses stone_brick_stairs (upside-down, y5 x51..54) because calcite_stairs is not in palette.json. `mcd check` reports the x51 and x54 ends as orphans; they sit against the front wall at z9.

Owner plot: porchWrap's front leg (z7..8, x85..94) overlaps the bay's z8 cells at x85..88. The plan has the bay and the porch on the same cells, so one of them has to move. The bay walls belong to P2; I only glazed the bay.
Roof duplication: porchDeep's shed roof and porchWrap's copper roof may collide with the roofs part (P3), so the merge will refuse one of them.

Shutter and vent flags: in-wall trapdoors (gin and church louvres, the barn vent slots) show as 'floating shutter' in `mcd fit` because the cell behind is interior air. Intentional, but the check needs an exception for vents.

Not run: `mcd walk` and `mcd approach` on the ways in. The ramps follow plan geometry (slab row z6 at y1, 2-cell landing at z7..8, porch deck as landing on the farmhouse and owner), but nothing has walked them.

Single-door cells are written by a local door() helper, and the granary's loft and back doors have no transom. The crib hatch is a pair of closed oak trapdoors, so it reads as a panel rather than an open hatch.
Elements not built here: the cupola louvres (P2/P3), the bay calcite (P2), the granary shell door pair (P2 shell, my doors only cover the openings), and the lancet stair heads (unverified).

waste.what: Glass panes, single doors and their connection states written cell by cell (about 60 g.set calls) for every window and door in the plot list.
waste.cost: roughly 60 hand-placed cells plus a retry after a bad sed edit; about 4 minutes
waste.tool: A window(g, {xs, ys, zs, along}) helper that sets pane connections, and a single door(g, x, y, z, facing, mat, hinge) helper in vocab, neither of which exists in h1-h4.

waste.what: Slab ramp coordinates worked out by hand for each plot, and the slabRamp helper cannot take stone_brick or stone_bricks because it writes block+'_slab' and the bare block name for the landing.
waste.cost: 5 ramps, each hand-written with a separate landing loop
waste.tool: slabRamp needs separate slab and landing material arguments (for example { slab: 'stone_brick', landing: 'stone_bricks' }) and a null landing for a porch deck that already serves as landing.

waste.what: Shutter placement against the window edges (outer shutters at x25/x28 and x31/x34 for 2-wide windows, z12/z16 for the school's tall windows) was worked out by hand. shutterPair places both sides of a single cell and would have put the wrong shutters on the school's windows.
waste.cost: about 10 shutter calls and a re-derivation of the offsets
waste.tool: A shutter helper that takes the window's extent (from x to x2, or from z to z2) and places shutters at each end, with an option for outer-only.

waste.what: Verifying shutters and vents against the fit check needed reading 51 'floating shutter' flags to separate the intentional in-wall vents from real errors.
waste.cost: one full read of `mcd fit` output and a manual filter
waste.tool: `mcd fit` should accept an exception list (for example --allow-in-wall-vent) or treat open trapdoors in the wall plane as vents.

companions.task: The five slab ramps and landings (school, farmhouse, church, granary, owner), the lancet sills, and the stone lintel stairs over the church door. Handed the ramp spec: bottom slabs on z6, a 2-long full-block landing at z7..8, and the stone_brick and stone_bricks palette ids.

The shutters and louvres (trapdoor shutters beside each window, the gin's wagon-door leaves, the barn vent slots, the belfry louvres) and the door hangs with hinges and transoms, so the frames and openings match the shell's cut-outs.

summary:
grounds: parts/grounds.mjs builds the lane (laneRow 0..95), all eight plot rings with gates and lantern posts, the ground patched in coarse dirt, podzol and rooted dirt, and gravel ways from each gate to the grade-floor doors (gin, forge, barn).
Yards: gin bales, schoolhouse bench and flower bed, farmhouse and owner flowers, forge wheel stand, cart, coal store and cordwood, church front-corner graveyard with picket, gate and headstones, barn cordwood ricks.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the grounds line shows 960 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. Lamps are only the ring lanterns.
polish: Cart: 7 of 8 bed trapdoors placed; the lean-to post (46,12) takes one cell. The wheels (open spruce_trapdoor at y2, z11) are flagged by `mcd fit` as floating shutters, a false positive for a wheel; a wheel block or closed pair is needed.
Graveyard: only the front corner (x55..58 z6..8) is picketed, gate at (55,1,7). The east strip x57..58 z9..17 has no picket (headstones take its cells per plan).
Not built: barrels in the gin yard, the stripping-shed work bench at x62 (barn plot), the cordwood at x69..70 z10..15 is built but the lean-to bench is not.
Lighting: only the ring lanterns (y4 at each front corner) and no lamp posts at the gates or on the gravel ways; the lamplighter's pass is still to do.
Ground patching: 25% coarse dirt across the pads with podzol and rooted dirt near fences, chosen by rng, not by design. Trees: none built.

Checks: `mcd check` shows no fault in my cells (its floating ladder, lectern, composter and orphan brick stairs are other parts'). `mcd fit` flags only the cart wheels (mine) and the owner stair hall (other part).

waste.what: Probing built cells one at a time with ad-hoc node scripts to find out which of my calls had been skipped (the cart post clash, the wheel stand, the graveyard gate and picket).
waste.cost: about 4 probe runs, each reading 16 to 30 cells by hand
waste.tool: A `mcd probe build.nbt --cells x,y,z ...` or a skipped-cell report from the vocab helpers (cart, wheelStand, picketYard) listed in make.sh output per part.

waste.what: Working out per-plot yard coordinates by hand from plan.md (gate line, path widths, bench and bale positions), and checking them against the ring and shell cells.
waste.cost: roughly 40 coordinate sets computed in my head; no check until make.sh ran
waste.tool: A plan-to-coordinates helper that reads plan.md's FACADES and YARD rows and emits the calls, or a `mcd yard-check` that flags a yard cell already taken by an earlier part before the build runs.

waste.what: Writing put()/groundAt() guards by hand so grounds only write into air or the ground fill and never into an earlier part's cells.
waste.cost: one helper file, reused in each part
waste.tool: A ground-writer in vocab (writeGround / writeIfAir) that applies the same rule for every part, with a skipped list returned to the caller.

waste.what: Gate placement: picketYard then g.unset then a gate write, because the picket writes a fence into the gate cell first.
waste.cost: one retry of the picket box shape
waste.tool: picketYard option { gate: [x, z] } that leaves the gate cell free and writes the gate with the correct facing.

waste.what: Checking the render by eye through zoom views to confirm the wheel stand, cart and gravel path read at all.
waste.cost: 2 zoom renders, 2 image reads
waste.tool: A `mcd zoom` batch mode with one view per named element from plan.md, so each element is checked in one call.

companions.task: Plant the yard properly: podzol and coarse-dirt patches under the trees and fences, a few real trees on the lowland edge, and grass-to-dirt transitions at the path edges, instead of the flat 25% coarse-dirt scatter I used.

Light the yards and the graveyard: lamp posts at the gates and along the gravel ways, a hanging lantern at the church picket gate, and a light check of the gin yard and the forge front after the shells are in.
Build the cart properly: wheels that stand on the bed as wheels (not open trapdoors that fit flags as floating shutters), the shafts and the post-clear east row for the cart under the lean-to.
Lay the headstones and mounds with real plinths and set the front-corner picket and gate in the graveyard, and decide the east strip's boundary with the headstones at x57..58.

summary:
room: gin wagon bay: Gin wagon bay furnished in parts/room-1.mjs (19 blocks, inside x 2..9, y 1..5, z 10..12): cotton-bale stack on the west wall as the focal piece, a tally desk with a stairs chair and barrels on the east, the x 4..7 wagon lane kept clear, two hanging lanterns over the bales and desk.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for this part. mcd room reports OK: 24 of 24 floor cells reachable, min light 8, 0 dark cells. Fit is OK, and the from-above render reads as a bale-and-desk bay.
The layout is one plan of fixed layers() rows, so it is easy to re-draw. Cotton bales are hay_block with white_concrete on top because palette.json has no white wool.
polish: Cotton bales use white_concrete tops (no white_wool in palette.json); if the owner wants true cotton texture, add white_wool to the gin palette.
The machine-room opening on z 13 is left open to the bay as the plan drew it; the bay furnishing keeps z 12 clear except the bales, barrels and chair, so the machine room stays unobstructed.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture cell and the candle/lantern/stair state keys by guessing their names and values (candles, hanging, facing/half) before running the build.
waste.cost: about 3 retries of the layout by reading the state names from the source of layers and the vocab; one build plus one room check to confirm.
waste.tool: `mcd states <block>` in the layers legend hint, or a `mcd room --suggest` mode that prints the exact state keys each legend block needs.

waste.what: Table made from a fence post plus a top slab, and chair from a stair, placed cell by cell in text rows.
waste.cost: ~6 cells hand-placed in one layers() call; the rest of the room text was fine.
waste.tool: A furnisher helper such as table(g, [x,y,z], material) and chair(g, [x,y,z], facing) in vocab that writes the fence + top slab and stair with correct states, and that checks the 'top' slab rule.

companions.task: Make the barrels of seed cotton and the oil cask: barrel facing, open states, and which barrels stand against the wall versus in the lane.
Confirm the machine room opening at z 13 and the gin shaft layout so the wagon bay's back row (z 12) leaves a clear route to the empty machine room.

summary: room: gin machine room: ["parts/room-2.mjs: gin machine room left as the clear bay the plan reserves (no furniture, posts or decor), lit by two lanterns hung from the loft floor at (3,5,14) and (8,5,14).", "`mcd room` says OK: all 24 floor cells reachable, light min 8, mean 9.3, 0 dark. `mcd check` flags nothing in x2..9 z13..15 (its only warnings are elsewhere in the build). make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt; this part placed 2 blocks, no REFUSED writes, no off-palette blocks."]
polish: Conflict between the trade brief and the spec: the trade asked for furniture, a focal piece and job sites, but plan.md RESERVED and the task's own spec say this room stays clear (no furniture, posts or decor, only wall lanterns). I followed the spec. If the owner wants furniture here, the bay's clear-path rule still holds.

plan.md's checklist has no room line (only P1-P6), and I was told to edit only my module, so I did not tick anything in plan.md or elements.md. The machine-room items there are already met: the room is clear, and every floor cell is at light 8 or more.

make.sh prints a stair-joiner warning ('nothing to step out onto at 86,6,9') from the chimneys/stairs part, outside my room. The build check also flags floating ladders at x52/x55 and a floating lectern and composter, all outside my box.

summary:
room: gin loft: Gin loft furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: hay store west with lanterns on the bales, cotton-sorting table (fence + top slab) and stair chair with a candle in the middle, focal cotton barrels at the back right under a standing lantern; fence rail round the shaft hole (7,6,14); lane kept clear from the hay door to the ladder landing.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the gin loft line shows 20 placed, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks.
mcd room says OK: 45/45 floor cells reachable, light min 8, 0 dark, 0 dim. mcd fit is clean for the loft; the remaining fit and check complaints are in other parts (church ladders, lectern, composter, a hallway).
polish: plan.md has no room-3 row in its checklist, and elements.md's 'loft bales/hay' item shares a line with the P5 ladder, so I did not tick either (other workers edit plan.md at the same time).
No cotton-bale or wool block is in palette.json, so the cotton store is barrels. Swap to a bale look if the palette gains one.
The roof has no trusses or ceiling block yet, so no hanging lantern: all lights are standing lanterns and a candle. Revisit once roofs.json exists.
The shaft hole at (7,6,14) is fenced on its four sides at floor level; the gin's ladder (2,1..6,15) and shaft frame are built by others and not checked here.

waste.cost: about 6 layout iterations, 2 rebuilds
waste.tool: A mcd plan option that prints the layers() rows with a per-cell label, or a helper that places named furniture by coordinate (e.g. furnish(g, room, [{block, at:[x,y,z]}])) and writes the text grid for you.

waste.cost: one read of palette.json and reasoning about substitutes
waste.tool: mcd blocks --check on a candidate list, plus a palette role with the cotton bale stand-in named, so the substitution is not decided by eye.

waste.what: Light fix: a corner at 7 needed a lantern; I found the spot from the room tool's suggestion and re-ran make.sh for a one-line change.
waste.cost: one rebuild
waste.tool: mcd room already suggests the lantern spot; a flag that writes the suggested lantern straight into the layer text would have saved the rebuild.

companions.task: Make the cotton bales (bale stacks of barrels or wool-look blocks) and the hay store, so the store reads as a cotton and hay loft rather than barrels.
Check the lantern placement against the light map and place one more hanging lantern from the roof trusses once the roof part exists, so the room's lighting is not only standing lanterns.
Confirm the ladder landing (2,7,15) above the hole and the loft shaft at (7,6,14) are safe to walk around once the gin's ladder and shaft are built, and cut any headroom the ladder needs.

summary:
room: schoolhouse cloakroom: Schoolhouse cloakroom furnished in parts/room-4.mjs: coat-hook fence pegs on the west column (y4), a boot bench (spruce stair seat plus a fence post carrying a standing lantern) on the east column; both doorway lanes and the west headroom stay clear.

plan.md has no per-room checklist line, so I ticked nothing there.
